podcast.title: Formation of Pez - July 1993
podcast.body: Ian received a phone call from Ben in July 1993, inviting him to start a new band with Ben, John, and Aaron. They held their first jam session in Ian's parents' basement that same month. "So our bands probably lasted a year each and then around July 1993. ... I got a phone call from Ben at one point and he was like me, Johnny and Aaron are thinking of starting a new band. Would you want to play with us? And so they all came over to my parents would let me jam in the basement. So they all came over and we had our first jam ever. Yeah. That was in July 1993."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Amp Anecdote with Kevin Gormley
podcast.body: At a high school talent show where Dragonflower and To Each His Own were playing, Ian couldn't find his guitar amp. Ben informed him that their guitar player, Kevin Gormley, had borrowed it to practice upstairs in the religion room, which marked Ian's first meeting with Ben. "And I remember right before about to go on stage, I couldn't find my guitar amp and I was like, guys, do you know, do you see a guitar amp missing anywhere? And Ben was like, oh, I think our guitar player boarded to go practice. ... And it was Kevin Gorewood taking my amp to go practice upstairs in the religion room ironically."

podcast.title: Dragonflower Member
podcast.body: Before joining Pezz, Ian D'Sa was a member of a band called Dragonflower, which played concurrently with To Each His Own in the 1990s. "That was 90. That was, I was in a different band called Dragonflower. The same time these guys were in a band called To Each His Own."

podcast.title: Golden Griddle Busboy
podcast.body: Ian D'Sa and Aaron Solowaniak both worked together as busboys at a Golden Griddle restaurant "way, way back in the day." "We both worked at Golden Griddle as busboys together way, way back in the day."

podcast.title: Joining the Band
podcast.body: Ian D'Sa, recognized as the best guitar player in their high school, was approached by Ben, John, and Aaron after they left To Each His Own, and agreed to join their new band. "And there was a guitar player in the school, this guy by the name of Ian DeSaw, who was by far leaps and bounds of Ascatar player in the school and a lovely guy. And so we sat and spoke with him. And he said that he wanted to hang out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Montreal Job and Commuting
podcast.body: During a difficult period for the band, Ian took a job in Montreal. He would commute back to Mississauga every other week to attempt to hold rehearsals, which often dwindled to just himself and Ben, with Aaron occasionally joining. "And I took a job in Montreal. ... So every second week and I drive home and, you know, try to get rehearsals going and stuff, which ended up at one point just being me and Ben and Aaron occasionally."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Ontario College of Art, Kelsey's Job
podcast.body: During the band's early years, Ian attended the Ontario College of Art and worked nights and weekends as a line cook and dishwasher at a Kelsey's restaurant. "At this point, I was going to the Ontario College of Art. And at nights and weekends, I worked at a Kelsey's as a line cook."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Returned from Montreal, Unemployment, Music Focus
podcast.body: After his job in Montreal, Ian returned to Mississauga, potentially on unemployment, which provided him a significant opportunity to focus solely on creating music. He then began showcasing new songs like "Try Honesty" and "Cut the Curtains" to the other band members. "And then it was when he left Montreal and came back and started doing, he, I think you were on unemployment or something. Yeah. They gave him a really good opportunity to work on music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Talent Show Meeting - Dragonflower vs. To Each His Own
podcast.body: Ian first met Ben Kowalewicz at a high school talent show where their respective bands, Dragonflower and To Each His Own, performed. He had previously met John and Aaron in classes. "The first time I met Ben was actually at a high school talent show. ... It was Dragonflower and To Each His Own plan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Try Honesty - Catalyst Song, Ian's Montreal Writing
podcast.body: While working in Montreal, Ian started writing the song "Try Honesty." He brought it back and showed it to Ben, and this song became a catalyst for a new era of the band, invigorating their creativity when it was primarily just Ian and Ben working on music. "And then, in try on, Wayne in Montreal, I started working on this song. They try honesty and came back and showed Ben. At this point, it was just me and Ben working on songs. And that song became like the catalyst for a new era of our band."

xref.title: Band Rebirth - Name Change, New Songs, New Rehearsal Space
xref.body: Following a period of struggles and individual pursuits, the band experienced a "rebirth." This was catalyzed by Ian D'Sa bringing in new songs like "Try Honesty" and "Cut the Curtains," Ben Kowalewicz suggesting a band name change (from Pezz to Billy Talent), and acquiring a new rehearsal space. "And then Ben suggested we change the band name and everything just kind of came together all at once and it did feel like a rebirth and we got a new rehearsal space down the front and sure burn over here and we felt like a real band again and was up."

xref.title: Ian's Parents' Basement - Milk Crate Storage
xref.body: Ian D'Sa's parents' basement served as a storage location for the milk crates and plywood used for their DIY stages. At one point, there were approximately 500 milk crates stored there, causing the basement to reek of spoiled milk. "I remember one time there was like 500 milk crates in Ian's basement and his mom would come down and say, Ian, what are you doing with all these milk crates? Don't worry, mom, it's all good. Well, my parents' basement wreaked like, like, like, broad milk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: No Lineup Changes
xref.body: Since its formation in 1993, the core lineup of Ben Kowalewicz, Ian D'Sa, John Gallant, and Aaron Solowaniak has remained constant, aside from some temporary situations. "Never. No. Never. That's insane. Yeah. There's been some temporary things here and there, but this has been the band."
